[page 100 / ... You with me.]
And thus the Arabs overtook him and killed him,
and returned in victory.
Likewise, those who had gone to the remaining quarters [also triumphed].
And fear of them fell upon all the kings.
And at that time the Persians departed from Egypt, and from Palestine, and from all the territories of the Romans.
And Shahrbaraz sent word to Heraclius,
and took an army for himself and killed Qardigan.
And he himself reigned for one year,
and was killed.
And after him, Baram (Boran?) daughter of Khosrow reigned over the Persians for a few months and died.
And her sister Azarmidokht reigned.
And within two years, many reigned.
And at this time, the Edessenes whom Khosrow had exiled
returned from Persia.
And Heraclius transgressed the law,
and took Martina, the daughter of his brother, as his wife,
and begot from her Heraclonas, an illegitimate son.
At this time an earthquake occurred in the month of Elul.
And a sign was seen in the sky coming from the south to the north,
resembling a spear,
and it remained for thirty days.
And this clearly portended the victory of the Arabs.
After Abu Bakr, 'Umar ruled {OCR?} for ten years.
This man sent a raiding force into Arabia,
and took Bostra captive.
And after a year he sent an army to Persia,
while the Persians were divided,
some of them indeed following Yazdegerd, the son of Khosrow,
and some of them following Hormizd.
And thus the Arabs prevailed over them,
and Hormizd was killed,
and Yazdegerd reigned.
Now Heraclius sent an army with Theodoric his brother against the Arabs.
And when they came to the district of Antioch, to the village of Gausit,
there was there a certain stylite and Chalcedonian, who said to Theodoric:
"Promise that you will wipe out those of the house of Severus,
and I will guarantee you victory."
He, however, replied:
"Even apart from your word, it is determined by me to persecute the Jacobites."
And when they arrived against the Arabs, the Romans struck camp (that is,
a camp?) entirely of his (of theirs?) near the Arabs.
And when they drew up in ranks against each other,
like rejected twigs they were cut off and trampled by the Arabs,
and the rest fled.
And the Arabs plundered the camp,
and grew very rich from the gold, silver, servants, and possessions that they found.
